# fm CLI coverage: what each read op does not report

Checked against fm 0.8.0 (29834929) on 2026-09-23. Reference: the Save as XML export of the Ooe solution.

Every probe below ran in one invocation:

```
fm --file=fmnet://localhost/ooe --username=admin --keychain --no-prompt --abort-on-error=false --out=/var/folders/1h/xw_j9f891q1_988625vlsw5c0000gp/T/fm-adt-oTVErS/batch.out.ndjson /var/folders/1h/xw_j9f891q1_988625vlsw5c0000gp/T/fm-adt-oTVErS/batch.ops.ndjson
```

302 kinds, 1557 attributes not reported.

### The biggest gaps

- **Layout parts** — fm 0.7.0 reported the part list at last, as `parts` on the layout itself: each part’s type, height, offset from the top of the layout, name, and a sub-summary’s break field with its occurrence. fm 0.8.0 adds the Part Definition dialog, which no read reached before it: `pagination` carries the page-break and page-numbering options — break before each occurrence, break after every N, restart page numbers, allow the part to break across page boundaries, discard the remainder — and the body also reports `rowState`, the alternate and active row state. Which members appear depends on the part type: a header, footer or title header carries `restartPageNumbers` alone. What is still unread is the numeric part-type code behind the type name, the part definition kind, the count of objects sitting in the band, and `pagination` itself on the three part types fm omits it for — top navigation, title footer and bottom navigation. (33 attributes across 10 kinds.)
- **File Options** — fm 0.8.0 adds a catalog for this, and it closes most of the gap: `read:fileOptions` answers with the startup layout, the minimum FileMaker version allowed to open the file, the login mode, the stored-credential and sign-in settings, the file icon, the spelling and text options, container thumbnail handling, and every file script trigger with its event, event code and script. What it still does not report is the two "don’t display in host’s file list" flags — one for FileMaker clients, one for WebDirect — the page setup saved with the file (orientation, scale and paper size), and whether a file script trigger is enabled in Browse mode. (13 attributes across 1 kind.)
- **Themes** — fm 0.7.0 has a theme catalog of its own: `read:theme` describe answers with the whole stylesheet as text, the five palette swatches, every named style’s key and display name, and the layouts using the theme. What it still does not say is where the theme came from and how FileMaker lays out on it — the base theme and base version a custom theme derives from, the locale, platform and theme version, the chart colour scheme, and the 25 layout-builder metrics the New Layout/Report assistant measures a new layout by. (35 attributes across 1 kind.)
- **Sort specifications** — A relationship’s sort order is readable in 0.7.0 — `rightToLeft.sortSpec.fields` names each level’s field and direction — but neither of its two switches is. `maintain` ("keep records in sorted order") is a confirmed gap: the reference file sets it and fm reports no such key. `blanksLast` is reported by no read either, though this file cannot prove fm never reports it — both of its sort specifications set it to false. Both keys are named on fm’s own write surface. A portal was further behind and is not any more: fm 0.8.0 reports a portal’s `sort.fields` — each level’s field as `Occurrence::Field` and its direction — and its `filter` formula as text, where every earlier build said nothing about a portal’s sorting, not even that it sorted. What a portal still withholds is the same pair a relationship does, `maintain` and `blanksLast`, plus any id for the sort field: fm names it and reports no field or occurrence id to resolve it by. (15 attributes across 4 kinds.)
- **Modification info** — Almost every catalog element in the export carries who changed it, when, and how many times. fm reports the triple on `layout` and nowhere else — `modified.by`, `modified.account` and `modified.timestamp` — leaving the other 39 kinds in this register with none of it, under any op. Still the most widely repeated gap here, and the narrowest to close: the shape fm already returns on a layout would answer it everywhere. (117 attributes across 39 kinds.)
- **Conditional formatting** — A layout object’s conditional formatting rules — the condition, the comparison value and the formatting each rule applies — are not reported, so a layout cannot be reproduced from what fm says about it. (32 attributes across 3 kinds.)
- **Calculation tokens** — fm 0.8.0 answers part of this at last. Sent the new `references: true`, `validate:calculation` returns the fields a formula refers to as {kind, name, occurrence, id} — the occurrence riding along with the field rather than being its own token — and its custom-function calls as {kind, name, id}. It is opt-in, and emitted only on the valid branch. Still named by nothing: variables, built-in functions, scripts, and plug-in functions. The plug-in case is the sharpest, because this build loads the installed plug-ins and so reports a formula calling one as valid while returning `references: []` for it — fm knows enough to accept the call and still will not say the call site is there. So "where is this field used" is answerable for fields and custom functions, and no further. (2 attributes across 2 kinds.)

## Packed words fm reports raw

100 kinds carry a packed options word that fm emits verbatim and decodes not at all: the raw number is present in the response, and none of the bits inside it is named.
The ask is the decode, not the number. FileMaker knows what each bit of each word means — the same table the Script Workspace uses to print a step’s options — and the register can only record which bits it has attributed by measurement.

## No read op exists

### calculation

Register id: `calculation-tokens`. Probe: `{"op":"validate:calculation","calculation":"Contacts::Name & $$SMTP Server","context":"Contacts","references":true}`.

**Not reported**

| Attribute | Known from | SaXML path |
|---|---|---|
| tokenised variable references of a formula | NOT REPORTED. fm 0.8.0-beta.0's `references` tokenises a formula's fields and its custom-function calls and nothing else: probed live on 2026-09-20, `Contacts::Name & $local & $$GLOBAL` returns the Name field alone, naming neither variable. So FileMaker's own VariableReference chunk has no counterpart here, and "which formulas read this $$ global" is answerable only by scanning calculation text. Keyed on the element field rather than on `references` itself so that the row CLOSES the day fm emits a variable token, rather than having to be noticed by a human first. The `variable` spelling is inferred from the two kinds fm does emit (`field`, `customFunction`); if fm chooses another word the row stays open, which understates coverage rather than overstating it | `DDR_INFO/Chunk[type=VariableReference]` |

Reported (4): `references`, `for`, `valid`, `contextResolved`.

Last checked fm 0.8.0 (29834929) on 2026-09-23; probe 74 of 75 in one invocation.

### calculation:plugin

Register id: `plugin-call-sites`. Probe: `{"op":"validate:calculation","calculation":"BE_Version","references":true}`.

**Not reported**

| Attribute | Known from | SaXML path |
|---|---|---|
| plug-in function call site in a formula | SaXML DDR_INFO writes a FunctionRef chunk for a call to a plug-in function. STILL A GAP in fm 0.8.0-beta.0 (29827611), and now for a sharper reason than before: this build loads the installed plug-ins (its stderr names BaseElements.fmplugin among four) and so parses `BE_Version` as a VALID formula, where 0.7.0 called it invalid with `table_missing` for an unresolvable reference. But asked with `references: true` — the key 0.8.0 added for exactly this question — the same probe returns `references: []`. fm therefore knows enough about the call to accept it and still will not say the call site is there, so a formula's plug-in call sites cannot be recovered from fm. | `DDR_INFO/Chunk[type=FunctionRef] (plug-in function)` |

Reported (4): `for`, `valid`, `references`, `contextResolved`.
